## Vocabulary

- **self**: Clustered collection insert locality (9/3)

## Definitions

- [statement] Large clustered keys can increase both collection storage and secondary-index storage. Secondary indexes refer to the clustered key's encoded RecordId, so clustering can trade the removed _id index against larger secondary-index references. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/clustered-collections/ · keywords: Clustered collection insert locality · also: https://hnasr.substack.com/p/mongodb-internal-architecture, https://dev.to/mongodb/mongodb-indexing-internals-showrecordid-and-hintnatural1-4cpl

## Structure and components

- [statement] Clustering removes one separately maintained _id structure, but that alone does not establish a throughput gain. Percona explicitly cautions that clustered writes may be slower, while MongoDB documents potential insert benefits and a random-key penalty; neither statement is a universal benchmark result. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/clustered-collections/ · keywords: Clustered collection insert locality · also: https://learn.percona.com/hubfs/eBooks/Percona_Mongo-Upgrade_Best_Practices.pdf

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The statement that MongoDB cannot store index-organized collections is obsolete as a blanket claim: the critical article itself adds a footnote acknowledging clustered collections beginning with MongoDB 5.3. Its ordinary-collection discussion should not be applied to explicitly clustered collections. (high confidence) — https://will-keleher.com/posts/mongo_performance_is_disk-graceful/ · keywords: Clustered collection insert locality · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/clustered-collections/
- [statement] The current manual requires a clustered index on { _id: 1 } and creation of that index when the collection is created. An existing ordinary collection cannot be converted in place; documents must be copied into another collection. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/clustered-collections/ · keywords: Clustered collection insert locality

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Cache capacity scopes the random-insert penalty. MongoDB describes eviction and replacement when random index entries no longer fit cache; combined with the clustered-document locality mechanism, this supports testing cache-resident and larger-than-cache workloads separately, rather than assigning a fixed UUID slowdown. This testing recommendation is an inference, not a measured clustered-collection result. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/faq/indexes.md · keywords: Clustered collection insert locality · also: https://dev.to/mongodb/mongodb-indexing-internals-showrecordid-and-hintnatural1-4cpl

## Facts and statements

- [statement] MongoDB clustered collections store documents in _id key order in one WiredTiger file, eliminating the separate default _id index. This makes application key order determine document placement. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/clustered-collections/ · keywords: Clustered collection insert locality · also: https://dev.to/mongodb/mongodb-indexing-internals-showrecordid-and-hintnatural1-4cpl, https://hnasr.substack.com/p/mongodb-internal-architecture, https://learn.percona.com/hubfs/eBooks/Percona_Mongo-Upgrade_Best_Practices.pdf
- [statement] With random UUIDv4 _id values, inserts into a clustered collection scatter document writes across the tree and reduce cache locality. Increasing keys concentrate insert activity; MongoDB recommends sequentially increasing clustered keys and warns that random keys may reduce performance. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/clustered-collections/ · keywords: Clustered collection insert locality · also: https://dev.to/mongodb/mongodb-indexing-internals-showrecordid-and-hintnatural1-4cpl
- [statement] For ordinary non-clustered collections, random _id values scatter the _id index entries without making document placement follow _id order. The document tree instead uses internal RecordIds; clustered collections derive an order-preserving RecordId from _id. (medium confidence) — https://dev.to/mongodb/mongodb-indexing-internals-showrecordid-and-hintnatural1-4cpl · keywords: Clustered collection insert locality · also: https://hnasr.substack.com/p/mongodb-internal-architecture, https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/storage/README.md, https://will-keleher.com/posts/mongo_performance_is_disk-graceful/
- [statement] Clustering eliminates the separate _id index: an _id lookup reaches the document through one tree traversal, and inserts avoid maintaining a second tree for that index. This describes logical tree work, not a guarantee of one physical disk I/O or the absence of journal and secondary-index writes. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/clustered-collections/ · keywords: Clustered collection insert locality · also: https://hnasr.substack.com/p/mongodb-internal-architecture, https://dev.to/mongodb/mongodb-indexing-internals-showrecordid-and-hintnatural1-4cpl
